definitions.explanation: A professional performer of {落語|らくご}, the traditional Japanese art of comic storytelling. The performer kneels alone on stage in a kimono, narrates a long humorous story, and plays all characters by changing voice and direction of gaze.

examples.japanese: {有名|ゆうめい}な{落語家|らくごか}が{出演|しゅつえん}した。
{彼|かれ}は{落語家|らくごか}になりたくて{弟子|でし}{入|い}りした。
examples.english: He wanted to become a rakugo performer, so he became an apprentice.

examples.japanese: {落語家|らくごか}は{扇子|せんす}と{手拭|てぬぐ}いだけで{多|おお}くの{登場人物|とうじょうじんぶつ}を{演|えん}じ{分|わ}ける。
examples.english: Rakugo performers play many different characters using only a fan and a hand towel.

notes:
Compound of {落語|らくご} (rakugo) + {家|か} (practitioner, professional). {落語家|らくごか} follow a strict ranking system: {見習|みなら}い → {前座|ぜんざ} → {二|に}つ{目|め} → {真打|しんうち}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {落語家|らくごか}になる: to become a rakugo performer
- {人気|にんき}{落語家|らくごか}: popular rakugo performer
- {落語家|らくごか}に{弟子入|でしい}りする: to apprentice oneself to a rakugo performer

CULTURAL NOTE:
A rakugo performer's stage name is given by their master and changes as they rise through the ranks. The two main professional associations are {落語協会|らくごきょうかい} and {落語芸術協会|らくごげいじゅつきょうかい} in Tokyo.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {芸人|げいにん}: entertainer; comedian — broader category that includes modern stand-up
- {噺家|はなしか}: storyteller — an older, more traditional term for the same profession
